subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student excels at breaking down complex problems logically, comparing and evaluating different pieces of information, and scoring well on traditional academic tests requiring analysis and judgement. In Sternberg's Triarchic Theory, this ability is called:
explanation: Analytical (componential) intelligence involves logical analysis, comparison, and evaluation — completing Sternberg's Triarchic Theory alongside Practical and Creative intelligence.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who is clever at everyday practical problem solving but only average at solving abstract academic puzzles is displaying, according to Sternberg's Triarchic Theory:
explanation: Practical (contextual) intelligence is the ability to adapt to and navigate real-world, everyday situations — distinct from analytical intelligence, which academic tests typically measure.
